newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends fragile, seen to move lower.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends fragile, seen to move lower.

text.p: The Philippine peso remained fragile on Friday, unnerved by the volatility in the region's currencies, traders said.
The market saw equities-related outflows and continued corporate demand for dollars.
"The oil firms started asking around for quotes in the afternoon," a dealer said.
The peso ended at 29.80 to dollar from the previous close of 29.48. It touched a low of 29.85 in the morning. Volume fell to $103.9 million from $150.8 million.
Again, the peso did not get any support from the central bank. "It was raising the selling rate every time the market moved up," a trader said.
Some dealers said the peso could still test its record low of 30, reached after it had a de facto devaluation on July 11.
"The Asian turmoil isn't over yet. It should last until next week," a second trader said.
